paper_metadata.title: Mechanical Properties and Microstructure Evolution of Cryorolled AlCoCrFeNi-Reinforced Aluminum Matrix Composites Tensile Tested at Room and Cryogenic Temperatures

evidence.quote: The AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy particles (HEAp)-reinforced aluminum matrix composites (AMCs) were fabricated by stir casting and subsequent cryorolling.
The AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy particles (HEAp)-reinforced aluminum matrix composites (AMCs) were fabricated by stir casting and subsequent cryorolling.

1.5, 3, and 4.5 wt pct HEAp/AMCs ingots were prepared by the stir casting process at 1073 K (Figure 1(a)).
Then, the synthesized ingots were extruded into 3.3 mm thick sheets at 713 K (Figure 1(b)).
To obtain HEAp/AMCs sheets with identical initial state before cryorolling except for mass fraction of HEAp, these sheets were annealed at 713 K for 1 hour.

They were cryorolled at 77 K in liquid nitrogen environment. The cryorolled HEAp/AMCs sheets with rolling reductions of 30, 60, and 90 pct (Figure 1(c)) were kept to analyze their mechanical properties.
